comment: Example client configs for laptops on the same LAN. Replace 'your-mac.local' with your host's mDNS name or LAN IP. The host serves FIVE lanes from one endpoint: 'heavy' + 'flash' + 'super-flash' (cloud) and 'local-orch' + 'local-sub' (host GPU). A lane name is the stable contract - the host can swap the model behind it without any client edit. Point the main model at a driving lane ('heavy' or 'local-orch') and the worker/subagent model at its cheap partner ('flash', 'super-flash', or 'local-sub'). Client bootstrap also installs `opencode-cloud`, `opencode-local`, and `opencode-super` profiles. Easiest of all: just run `ferry opencode` on the client to write the opencode block below automatically (it detects whatever the host is serving). Every generated config also carries a fleet-identity `headers` map under `options` — `X-Ferry-Client` (this machine's name) and `X-Ferry-Fleet` (from `$FERRY_FLEET`, for a one-shot pin) — which `ferry opencode` / `ferry claude` write for you; see the `options` block below for the shape.

opencode._tip: Or just run `ferry opencode` on the client to write this automatically.

generic_openai_sdk_python.code:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url='http://your-mac.local:8090/v1',
    api_key='local'
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model='orch',
    messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Tell me a joke.'}]
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
